Today we celebrate Juneteenth, the day in 1865 when the last enslaved people in America finally learned they were free.

Juneteenth is a reminder of both how far this country has come and how much more we can do for everyone as a nation. The promise of freedom and equality for all Americans has never been fully realized, and the work of making it real continues.

In Congress, I continue to fight to make sure the people of California’s 19th Congressional District have access to the opportunities, rights, and protections that they deserve. That work is rooted in the belief that this country is strongest when every person has that opportunity.

Today, we honor the resilience and contributions of Black Americans who have fought for that freedom through generations of struggle and sacrifice. Their story is America’s story, and it deserves to be remembered not just today, but every day.

Let’s honor Juneteenth by recommitting ourselves to the work of building a more just and equal country for everyone..

Sincerely,
Jimmy

subject: SIX DAYS LATER, FLEMING STILL WON'T SAY WHETHER HE HAS RESIGNED FROM DC LOBBYING FIRM
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
New ethics law prohibits statewide elected officials from being paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZGUiTCfGTTG?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEJune 19, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**SIX DAYS LATER, FLEMING STILL WON'T SAY WHETHER HE HAS RESIGNED FROM DC LOBBYING FIRM** _New ethics law prohibits statewide elected officials from being paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Six days after Governor Jeff Landry signed House Bill 210 into law prohibiting statewide elected officials from being paid to lobby, advise, or consult while serving in office, State Treasurer John Fleming has yet to say whether he has resigned from the Washington lobbying firm that pays him or whether he intends to step down from office.
The law has immediate implications for Fleming, who joined The McKeon Group, a Washington lobbying and consulting firm, as a registered lobbyist in 2021 and remains listed as an advisor. During the Louisiana U.S. Senate debate, Fleming acknowledged that he receives monthly payments from the firm while simultaneously serving as Louisiana State Treasurer.
According to Fleming's financial disclosure forms, he received more than $40,000 from The McKeon Group in 2024 while also collecting a taxpayer-funded salary from the State of Louisiana.
Despite the law taking effect nearly a week ago, Fleming has not publicly announced whether he has severed ties with the firm or how he intends to comply with the new ethics requirements.
_"Six days have passed, and John Fleming still hasn't given the people of Louisiana an answer,"_**said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.**_"The law is clear. Statewide elected officials cannot be paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office. If John Fleming wants to remain State Treasurer, he should resign from the McKeon Group. If he wants to remain on the payroll of a Washington lobbying firm, he should resign as State Treasurer."_
Governor Landry and the Legislature acted to strengthen Louisiana's ethics laws and prohibit arrangements that allow statewide elected officials to simultaneously serve in public office while being paid by lobbying and consulting firms.
To date, Fleming has not publicly stated which path he intends to take.

body:
Plus: Only 29% of Democrats are still proud to be American. | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/16zmDoilmuU?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | At two New Mexico smoke shops, most of what's on the shelves isn't food.
Somehow, they're now among the biggest SNAP retailers in the state. And the state is about to find out who's paying for it.
[Then Harry Enten put a number on national pride this week.](https://us.list-manage.com/19kP55ZdHiv?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) The Democratic side of the chart is unrecognizable.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/81B1giyXLve?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔥 **SNAP FRAUD: TWO NM SMOKE SHOPS RAKED IN $878K**
One pulled in $435,999. The other pulled in $442,539. About seven times what an average convenience store sees in a year. Their own online profiles include 81 photos of inventory. Want to guess how many showed something a SNAP card can legally buy?
Two. Water and soda.
**Sen. Pat Woods just sent USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins a letter that names names and lays out the timeline. We walk through the receipts.

** 🇺🇸 **ONLY 29% OF DEMOCRATS ARE PROUD TO BE AMERICAN**
In 2001, the number was 85%. Today it's 29%. That's a collapse.
Harry Enten laid out the data on displaying the American flag, what July 4th means, and national pride.
Mark shares what a friend learned in a UNM classroom recently when he asked one simple question about the American system. Not one student would concede the point. This is what the next generation is being taught. And we go there.
---
| [Stream No Doubt About It Podcast Now](https://us.list-manage.com/E8c1_u9cQU1?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 🏔️ **MAYOR BJ LINDSAY ON THE BUILDER WHO'S DONE WITH NEW MEXICO**
Angel Fire Mayor BJ Lindsay joined us this week — and he didn't pull punches.
Abrazo Homes co-founder Mackenzie Bishop just told the Albuquerque Journal that launching operations in Texas is a "near weekly temptation." The permit numbers explain why. Texas issued 16,572 building permits in April. New Mexico issued 583. Lubbock County outbuilt Bernalillo with half the population.
BJ's been a general contractor in NM long enough to know exactly why this is happening — and what Angel Fire just pulled off with workforce housing that proves it doesn't have to.
Plus a Mark vs the Mountain episode 5 reveal you'll want to see.

| **U.S. to Intervene in Judicial Watch’s Reparations Lawsuit****[](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=38075&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1XS0pfUVZtcFUtMCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3287cc24ac2219c56ae972d6ab08892aba5c452f9c501ff9431bc7c5d7d3b95b)**The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a[motion to intervene](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=38054&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZsaW5uLWV0LWFsLXYtY2l0eS1vZi1ldmFuc3Rvbi11c2EtaW50ZXJ2ZW50aW9uLTA0MjY5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=55ef0c15862baa713d4ae311bf573cdc7652b3f7a92a193fa5ede10e776e6f95) in our class action civil rights lawsuit challenging the City of Evanston’s reparations program, which makes $25,000 direct cash payments to black residents and descendants of black residents who lived in Evanston, Illinois, between 1919 and 1969.The United States filed its motion and a proposed complaint in intervention in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois in our May 2024 [lawsuit](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=32489&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvcmVwYXJhdGlvbnMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=e2f17164aa218b80367569984ffc689ca37a00bd814f1152d75d97e5366734ad) ([_Flinn et al. v. City of Evanston_](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=32473&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZsaW5uLXYtZXZhbnN0b24tcmVwYXJhdGlvbi1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDQyNjkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=ef1226e71ba572063d1d869b1a65efa1ea5da643866093e9278f934964277209) (No. 1:24-cv-04269)). We are assisted by Christine Svenson of Svenson Legal, LLC.The Justice Department’s proposed complaint in intervention names the City of Evanston as a defendant and alleges that the program violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. The Justice Department also alleges the program violates the Fair Housing Act.The United States asserts that it has an unconditional right to intervene under Section 902 of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. § 2000h-2, which allows the attorney general to intervene in cases alleging the denial of equal protection of the laws on account of race when the case is certified to be of general public importance. body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133656956/628661050/1231236074?refcode=RS_EM_EN_2026.06.19_Juneteenth&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiODQ5YmU5Ni01MjZjLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xd4VkE93b9GWMux3IuRrABhWoZDcslsdVrl9OV8kPok=&emci=51813aa2-386c-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=b849be96-526c-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=23483442) | Hi Peter, Walking through our local Juneteenth celebration today, I reflected on two truths. 1) Our country was built on so much hatred and violence and cruelty — no matter how much this Administration tries to erase the truth. 2) The story of Black America is also one of joy and resiliency and love and community. **Today marks 160 years since the news of emancipation reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally ending chattel slavery in the United States.** From that day on, lawmakers have tried time and time again to develop systems that disenfranchise and dehumanize Black Americans. To gut the Voting Rights Act, to deny military officer commendations, to strip funding from Black Maternal Health programs, and to attack our safety net. And with every vile, racist attempt, it is people — coming together in community and solidarity — that keep us moving forward. **This Juneteenth, I celebrate that history of resilience and commit to continuing to work arm in arm with Black activists, civic leaders, and neighbors who seek to redress past and present sins of this country in pursuit of a more just America.** ❤️💚🖤 — Emily | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. She grew up in a working-class Union household in Port Orchard and was the first in her family to attend college. clean_body: | Hi Peter, Walking through our local Juneteenth celebration today, I reflected on two truths. 1) Our country was built on so much hatred and violence and cruelty — no matter how much this Administration tries to erase the truth. 2) The story of Black America is also one of joy and resiliency and love and community. Today marks 160 years since the news of emancipation reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally ending chattel slavery in the United States. From that day on, lawmakers have tried time and time again to develop systems that disenfranchise and dehumanize Black Americans. To gut the Voting Rights Act, to deny military officer commendations, to strip funding from Black Maternal Health programs, and to attack our safety net. And with every vile, racist attempt, it is people — coming together in community and solidarity — that keep us moving forward. This Juneteenth, I celebrate that history of resilience and commit to continuing to work arm in arm with Black activists, civic leaders, and neighbors who seek to redress past and present sins of this country in pursuit of a more just America. ❤️💚🖤 — Emily | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. | | Dear Peter,

Today is Juneteenth, the day we celebrate the end of the Civil War and the smashing of slavery, one of the most brutally oppressive systems the world has ever known. American capitalism was built on the exploitation of enslaved Black people and the genocide of indigenous peoples. The horrors of slavery, Jim Crow segregation, and the ongoing exploitation of Black working people have provided unimaginable wealth for a tiny elite, while impoverishing generations of Black Americans and their communities.
The end of slavery was not won by the voices of “moderation,” who at the time argued for a kinder, gentler form of slavery and for a process of gradual change, and who derided abolitionists as divisive and uncouth people. This victory did not belong to those who attached themselves to the two parties of American capitalism, at that time the Whig Party and the Democratic Party, both of which defended the system of slavery. It did not belong to the Uncle Toms of the day. Instead, it belonged to the Black, brown and white troops who courageously fought and defeated the slave-owning class on the battlefields. And yes, it was a multi-racial struggle that succeeded in crushing the white slaveholders.
While slavery was defeated, the horrors of institutional racism were not. That is why our antiwar pro-worker Congressional campaign is fighting against racism and all oppression.
**Neither of the Democrats running in this race, Adam Smith and Melissa Chaudhry, even mention the needs of the Black community on their campaign websites.** Kshama is the only candidate in this race fighting for Black working-class and poor people and the only candidate with the track record of winning victories for the Black community.
Kshama is fighting for reparations for Black working-class and poor people, funded by taxing the rich. The net worth of the top one percent of the United States is at a shocking [$55 trillion](https://us.list-manage.com/cW6Arh20zLG?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15). We need to tax the rich to fund massive investment in Black and historically Black communities. We need quality affordable housing in Black communities, and strong national rent control. We need free public college and university, including a major increase in funding for Historically Black Colleges & Universities (HBCUs) and an expansion of community colleges in Black neighborhoods. We need to build free public healthcare clinics in every Black community as part of a free national healthcare system. We need to expand mass transit and make it free, including by ensuring high-quality, frequent, accessible public transit routes in every Black community.
Kshama is fighting for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee funded by taxing the rich. As part of this, Kshama is also calling for a national program to create hundreds of thousands of jobs for Black workers to help carry out the critical work of rebuilding infrastructure, expanding mass transit, and transforming our energy system.
We need to end mass incarceration, ban for-profit prisons, and stop forced, unpaid, and low-wage prison labor. We need to bring an end to racist policing and put police departments under the control of democratically elected community boards with full power over department policy, hiring, and firing. We need to put an end to the disastrous “war on drugs,” and instead fund healthcare, housing, education, and support for small businesses alongside a major expansion of living-wage union jobs.
Democratic Congressmember Adam Smith, who is Kshama’s main opponent, has had a long record of slashing hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicare, Medicaid, social services, and public housing. He was also one of the many Democrats who voted for the bailouts of the billionaires in the wake of the 2008 Great Recession. The bailout policies plundered the millions of working people who faced home foreclosures and handed over tens of billions of dollars worth of real estate to private equity. This bipartisan robbery against working people is a big reason why rents have been skyrocketing. All of these policies voted for by Adam Smith have disproportionately and severely undermined the living standards of Black working-class and poor people.
As the only socialist on Seattle’s City Council, Kshama Sawant led the fight to win the Amazon Tax, which funds hundreds of millions of dollars of affordable housing every year by taxing big corporations like Amazon. Kshama also campaigned for housing justice for Black working and poor people alongside “an expansive coalition of nonprofit organizations, faith-based institutions, and affordable housing providers,” including hosting a [major rally](https://us.list-manage.com/15aS0LZd9lW?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) for “reparations, unity, and affordable housing” in the summer of 2021. Kshama’s office used that public momentum to dedicate [millions of dollars](https://us.list-manage.com/Xw85RgDEFCz?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) of the Amazon Tax she won in 2020 specifically towards building [housing for the Black community](https://us.list-manage.com/ZT6RLeK0IAU?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) in Seattle’s historically Black Central District, a form of reparations. She also helped win $500,000 to fund the [Garfield Super Block and community center](https://us.list-manage.com/Zx0vFmEQMM7?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) in the Central District. She helped organize Black and other marginalized-community tenants at [Chateau Apartments](https://us.list-manage.com/JfRMScM7Yy3?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) and [Rainier Court](https://us.list-manage.com/19q7U_2o6JO?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) to successfully fight and win against the mass evictions and rent increases attempted by their exploitative landlords. We need to organize millions of people around the country and build a movement to win these kinds of victories on a much larger scale. Through her annual People’s Budget campaign, Kshama won full public funding for [legal defense](https://us.list-manage.com/hpLGAWlJZzB?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) for any working-class renters facing eviction. Statistical evidence indicates that Black community members, particularly women, disproportionately face evictions and that trained legal counsel dramatically increases the likelihood of preventing evictions.
The greatest material improvement in the lives of Black American workers came through the mass labor movements of the 1930s and 1940s and the creation of the Congress of Industrial Organizations, which built fighting multiracial unions and helped to power the Civil Rights movement. We need to rebuild a fighting, anti-racist labor movement.
In solidarity,Kshama for Congress

clean_body: End the War on Black People! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Kshama Sawant is the ONLY candidate in WA's 9th Congressional District race who has beaten the billionaires. Kshama is also the ONLY candidate in the race fighting to win free healthcare for all funded by taxing the rich , to end all military aid to Israel , to stop the AI data centers and mass layoffs , and for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee. | | | JOIN US FOR OUR JUNE VOLUNTEER DAY THIS SATURDAY, JUNE 20th AT 11:00AM Judkins Park Light Rail Station, SeattleOthello Light Rail Station, SeattleFederal Way Farmers Market | | | Not in Seattle, or can't make it to Volunteer Day? or sign up for another sign up for another ! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Dear Peter, Today is Juneteenth, the day we celebrate the end of the Civil War and the smashing of slavery, one of the most brutally oppressive systems the world has ever known. American capitalism was built on the exploitation of enslaved Black people and the genocide of indigenous peoples. The horrors of slavery, Jim Crow segregation, and the ongoing exploitation of Black working people have provided unimaginable wealth for a tiny elite, while impoverishing generations of Black Americans and their communities. The end of slavery was not won by the voices of “moderation,” who at the time argued for a kinder, gentler form of slavery and for a process of gradual change, and who derided abolitionists as divisive and uncouth people. This victory did not belong to those who attached themselves to the two parties of American capitalism, at that time the Whig Party and the Democratic Party, both of which defended the system of slavery. It did not belong to the Uncle Toms of the day. Instead, it belonged to the Black, brown and white troops who courageously fought and defeated the slave-owning class on the battlefields. And yes, it was a multi-racial struggle that succeeded in crushing the white slaveholders. While slavery was defeated, the horrors of institutional racism were not. That is why our antiwar pro-worker Congressional campaign is fighting against racism and all oppression. Neither of the Democrats running in this race, Adam Smith and Melissa Chaudhry, even mention the needs of the Black community on their campaign websites. Kshama is the only candidate in this race fighting for Black working-class and poor people and the only candidate with the track record of winning victories for the Black community. Kshama is fighting for reparations for Black working-class and poor people, funded by taxing the rich. The net worth of the top one percent of the United States is at a shocking . We need to tax the rich to fund massive investment in Black and historically Black communities. We need quality affordable housing in Black communities, and strong national rent control. We need free public college and university, including a major increase in funding for Historically Black Colleges & Universities (HBCUs) and an expansion of community colleges in Black neighborhoods. We need to build free public healthcare clinics in every Black community as part of a free national healthcare system. We need to expand mass transit and make it free, including by ensuring high-quality, frequent, accessible public transit routes in every Black community. Kshama is fighting for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee funded by taxing the rich. As part of this, Kshama is also calling for a national program to create hundreds of thousands of jobs for Black workers to help carry out the critical work of rebuilding infrastructure, expanding mass transit, and transforming our energy system. We need to end mass incarceration, ban for-profit prisons, and stop forced, unpaid, and low-wage prison labor. We need to bring an end to racist policing and put police departments under the control of democratically elected community boards with full power over department policy, hiring, and firing. We need to put an end to the disastrous “war on drugs,” and instead fund healthcare, housing, education, and support for small businesses alongside a major expansion of living-wage union jobs. Democratic Congressmember Adam Smith, who is Kshama’s main opponent, has had a long record of slashing hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicare, Medicaid, social services, and public housing. He was also one of the many Democrats who voted for the bailouts of the billionaires in the wake of the 2008 Great Recession. The bailout policies plundered the millions of working people who faced home foreclosures and handed over tens of billions of dollars worth of real estate to private equity. This bipartisan robbery against working people is a big reason why rents have been skyrocketing. All of these policies voted for by Adam Smith have disproportionately and severely undermined the living standards of Black working-class and poor people. As the only socialist on Seattle’s City Council, Kshama Sawant led the fight to win the Amazon Tax, which funds hundreds of millions of dollars of affordable housing every year by taxing big corporations like Amazon. Kshama also campaigned for housing justice for Black working and poor people alongside “an expansive coalition of nonprofit organizations, faith-based institutions, and affordable housing providers,” including hosting a for “reparations, unity, and affordable housing” in the summer of 2021. Kshama’s office used that public momentum to dedicate of the Amazon Tax she won in 2020 specifically towards building in Seattle’s historically Black Central District, a form of reparations. She also helped win $500,000 to fund the in the Central District. She helped organize Black and other marginalized-community tenants at and to successfully fight and win against the mass evictions and rent increases attempted by their exploitative landlords. We need to organize millions of people around the country and build a movement to win these kinds of victories on a much larger scale. Through her annual People’s Budget campaign, Kshama won full public funding for for any working-class renters facing eviction. Statistical evidence indicates that Black community members, particularly women, disproportionately face evictions and that trained legal counsel dramatically increases the likelihood of preventing evictions. The greatest material improvement in the lives of Black American workers came through the mass labor movements of the 1930s and 1940s and the creation of the Congress of Industrial Organizations, which built fighting multiracial unions and helped to power the Civil Rights movement. We need to rebuild a fighting, anti-racist labor movement. **For more information, please visit:[wisgop.org/calendar/events/](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail19.com/t/y-l-flkjiht-didthutlhu-j/) ** **Green County**
The Republican Party of Green County joined with Dane and Rock Counties for a stellar tri-county Pints and Politics night on Tuesday, June 2. Attendees heard from an array of first-class guest speakers. Members also attended a Memorial Day Service at the Brooklyn Area Veterans Memorial, hosted by Chairman John Fandrich. **Green Lake County**
Attendees at the annual June Dairy Days Parade in Markesan on Saturday, June 13th saw Republicans of Green Lake walking with their classic Elephant Float! **Monroe County**
Monroe County Republicans were out in force on June 6th at the Monroe County Dairy Breakfast, showing strong support for their local and state-wide candidates and standing with the farmers who keep communities thriving. It was a great morning at the Trescher Farm in Cashton, celebrating agriculture, neighbors, and the values that make Monroe County strong.

The Sparta Butterfest parade had a number of attendees, including Rep. Nancy VanderMeer, Secretary of State candidate Nate Pollnow, Sheriff Wes Revels, and Sheriff candidate Chris Weaver. **Sauk County**
Republicans of Sauk County sponsored and hosted a joint Flag Day / Trump Birthday Party this past Sunday, the 14th. The party was a hit. **St. Croix County**
Republicans of St. Croix absolutely jam-packed their last two weeks, putting in incredible work for conservatism in the county. Several members attended the Trump Roundtable in Chippewa Falls, and other members packed up to represent at back-to-back parades, the Somerset Pea Soup Day Parade and the Baldwin Windmill Days Parade. Rob Kreibich for Assembly came in for reinforcement during the Windmill Days Parade. To finish it all off, St. Croix County Republicans participated in a flag wave for President Trump's birthday and Flag Day. **Pepin County**
Pepin County showed up for our country this past Flag Day: 30 of their members volunteered their Sunday to wave flags and celebrate birthdays (America's 250th and President Trump's 80th). The patriots were met with cheers and honks from drivers passing by. Peter,

The primaries are over. The two parties have chosen their nominees. **Now the people of Maine have a choice to make.** Do we want more partisan politics, more division, and more excuses? Or do we want a Governor who answers only to the people of Maine? That’s why I’m running as an independent.

Today is the first day of the general election campaign. If you believe Maine deserves a Governor who answers only to its people, not political insiders, now is the time to step in.

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | | • | Behind the Markets ---|--- | • | Weiss Ratings Plus ---|--- | • | Salem Media Group ---|--- | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ## Truce in Lebanon as Talks Stall
A U.S.-backed [ceasefire took effect](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQBuCngc3IHOCEwUMXtnTtiM72kTi92Mg2oenTV-QVOp5O-vV__9dlvqBnH66f-CBdljgH2jNTKZRmnzDcKa6YnP-lXJC_cy6boxkkKCGVADk79Pya-9rphQioq0m3p3M7DrJVfX3TbugMyU6NEi2dR6ST7ReyqhvQDdZA7fWRJhXIVsoRoDG4GAIYBmWMoXNf9ZKcLzE19-hDudHCr_ik1Nj4qFnfSllz1X1UMFUw7fveLPHnUBz_Cib2TxLHXcG0ZXGgxEpoSThCFmGzTJjEWyfWmMsaAznhc0JiwWQwxCBsDAt7W8R9CyTasU7arbtn9lmdql5eH-j53aj8a8anhr8AAAD__2goixM) between Israel and Hezbollah on Friday afternoon, hours after Israeli forces struck more than 80 targets in southern Lebanon, where four Israeli soldiers and at least 18 civilians were killed. Each side accused the other of violating the truce within hours. The fighting had already derailed the wider U.S.-Iran framework signed midweek: next-phase nuclear [talks were postponed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOpCAUBeCnwQ6DV8TfgmIbu9l2S3ORqzKLYADHzDz9xnmFrU9ycr7z5zE90HkX1t-4ky5LnAJd2VMplCaXMDwpHpis-1Au6P_mXE5LEwhQXCgOYrLo_HuSldULEVBbkW76n2boRKNktWkJvVIoBgt27jsBQi62lQMamg3KFiun7zahQDRCDAC1wcUQQNcpYwz9SCYFWVdiqp_RhbLR4t_xRame4155vZVyZNb-YjAyGK_rqmeTb8WdMxi9exE_D4uFMoPxRvEz8wsT_4p4PvNBwZLlJZ37wfd4cpcTkueeDIYY-EYfE73HjS9u3YoLK4OxStoel_PeZdUzKdYdnf-OKv_15EvDvwAAAP__gX2L6A), and the vice president scrapped a trip to Switzerland. Iran's Revolutionary Guard separately declared the Strait of Hormuz [closed again](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ8Gd0R4g3FcUFzjLtdeaS1miUmwsWCTKHn6k_9X-JtpRvo03_y7TleMKW63v7iS5ZCnjd41ETOVKRbc7pR3LD5-qTKmR6389DSBAiOVkaAmjzF9Jt14G4iAzg3Ztr-0Q6dao5vFKhqMw163zqizvnSkPQyAvaZudkPrm2gPmjKgWqUGgJPD4Aig64xzji5aaEU-ci6ne44bLxTSJ7-onOa8NskuzHsV5z8CRgHj9tlz5aMSMB5gAaM6oh0EjO9ckpeHooDx0JOe5oSFquSFZOWCkWUOcsllfX7lnHIlL_GGcZMYmIp8Vpli4CpdyvMDPQkYm2L9_o4pxWp6odVtxZh-5vGvPn1Z-B8AAP__YxaL7Q), though Washington said tanker traffic through the waterway was surging.
## White House Bids Old Jet Farewell
White House staff bid farewell to the 35-year-old Boeing 747 that has flown as Air Force One since 1990, [posting tributes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO4yAUgOHT4I4IP4OxC4pt3GXbLS0wj_hlMVhAEmVOP8pcYepf-or_33W9WoqUbn_tgaaFvCZ81YitYVmp2HTHfNri6Qtrs_F_re3hcQUBIxcjB7F6S_G9ys6bgAg4dGh6PfWzEv0ou904NcOgnPYKIMDspB6lmjQMvbD95EJH5qOJEUQvxAxwcTY4BFBqdM7hJJkU6KnlcrlnSm3HEN_5ieWy5aOLZm_trGz4w2BhsLQdd4rx0xgsZ460vRksHgOmigwWNQ_9PAG3VHjIZUOeE3KXkdKNa6l5K4_j5M-Ng7IMlq4Yf74oRqqjZlLcDks_fNd-9etp4DsAAP__7xN9gA) and calling its return trip from Europe this week "The Last Ride." The Air Force pushed back, saying the aging jet is not being retired and will keep serving alongside a Qatari-donated 747 set to take over as a temporary Air Force One as soon as next month. The president is weighing whether to take that plane's [first flight](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2OpjAQe5rQBYX5CD9Fimvo9torUSATmL0hQUn40N7Tn9hXWMmSZVmybP_5mD8sMYXttz3QFB_ngHdmLAXTTMmGT4ynTY7-YS6W_-ZcLoczKOik6iSo2Vnir7mtnPGIgK8KTdMPzahV07XVbvpBP2hGPfoRVTNoPfi-d9ivgAOMFZknTXWgGqVGgHqxfkEArbtlWXBoRavQUYmp_owUyo6ev-IbU73Go2Kzl3Jm8folYBIw3fddh2V9Vjy-gOmMTIXWLGByMVh2sqTrOAVM3yyPizlLCvbarmRZeqZtLzLgLS0l6WNaUcaA8ohXKDJdeT9iQolvfOQa7Ksdh15XybjzJmbKXS9atR2W-Ltj-dGxbwP_AwAA__-_dJAd) to Mount Rushmore on July 3. The outgoing jet has carried six presidents, beginning with George H.W. Bush. The three incoming [jets will wear Trump's preferred](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ8GOwz-ImpBcY3dXnulAf3Z_fdQCLCavae_eK9w3SSTmcl8X7f5ZsjTfv80G-riwrzjmT2WgmmmZPYnhmjSSj-Yi_HfOZfXijMIUFwoDmJeDfn3LKtVO0TAtkLd9EMzdqJRsnropu1HHBqhpFTSLW27jAak6px1PcBgK9JXm1AgGiFGgNoaZxGg65S1FgfJpMCVSkj1M9BeHuj8OxyY6iVsldePUmJm7QeDicF0nme92Hy9uHwG0yUZTC-euaHEXUgL8oMij97syJ1HLLyk1xZ5NLQXvgQf0hWpkl7jSd5TVj2T4r4Z8n-r5V-oDg2_AQAA___-UX7O) red, white, gold, and navy scheme.
## TSA to World Cup Fans: Check the Ranch
American ranch dressing has become a breakout star of the World Cup, and now the TSA is weighing in on the [ranch craze](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMR3ReAADhYvb0OW2W6IBhjBZx0ZmNlHy9KvkFbb9j_QV5-s8nkmCxMt_urHXNY2RH0dgVc6jZIpXTjvlRV58KIXv49CfhUcEdCW4EmFcSMJzrIvFr8zIVcHetp3tG7CuLjZfU1Vhh2y5rabWLs0K_dw5BJrtujooxL81cAgWoEc8TbROjNg0bpom7mpTAy-iKZ-uSaJuvIZnunM-zelWBL-p7oep_hkcDA668SYhvDeDw56CzM93zhSPPWUllRQNDk1f2Rr6UqJyjp9KocwU562cM73Y4FBkv-wPCUEO15oaLjeSj1zon666e_wNAAD__wPwfmg).
